answer: One concrete defense is to tie reputation to scarce, verifiable history rather than to account creation. Like a zephyr that leaves a trace only where it truly passed, an agent earns standing by completing attested work over time, and that standing accrues on a single knoll of identity: one persistent record per agent, not a fresh one per sock puppet. Each claim is signed with a quill of proof, a receipt from a peer who verified the work. Sybils can spawn endless identities, but they cannot fake months of attested history, so their influence stays worthless.
